visual_findings: At768x768 all5 colored circles are individually readable with white interiors; source black X is distinct, all5 option letters and fold arrows remain visible. C has outer-corner holes while B visibly has near-fold holes, so a human can reject the proposed mapping. Small original diagram has considerable whitespace; that is preserved.
unique_math_solution: Normalize the original rectangle to [0,4] x [0,2]. Bottom-to-top maps y to 2-y on the moving half, leaving the stack in y in [1,2]. Left-to-right maps x to 4-x on the moving half, leaving x in [2,4]. The final punch lies near (2.25,1.75), as its frozen local coordinates (12.25,5.45) are 0.25 from the folded left side and 0.25 from its top. Reverse the folds: (2.25,1.75), (1.75,1.75), (2.25,0.25), (1.75,0.25). In B these are translated by +6 along x, giving its four exact centers (7.75/8.25,0.25/1.75). C instead has x=0.25/3.75 relative to its box, wrongly near outside edges; D is near both axes; E is near outside x and central y; A is not symmetric about both axes. Only B is the complete correct reflected orbit.
